payload.comment: Training stage is clean and internally consistent. No deterministic findings. Key verifications: (1) Model family is tiny_cnn (CNN); transformer-specific fields (num_heads, patch_size, positional_encoding, tokenizer_layers, mlp_ratio, pooling) are present in the config but are inert for CNN families and do not constitute a hybrid. (2) All augmentations in use (hflip, brightness, contrast) are built-in primitives requiring no extension approval. (3) Data audit passed all checks: official split, disjoint train/val (overlap=0), test not inspected, train_stats_only=true. (4) Training converged over the full 15-epoch budget: train loss decreased monotonically (0.563→0.305), val accuracy rose from 0.954 to 0.990 with expected epoch-to-epoch noise; no overfitting signal. (5) Cosine LR schedule correctly anneals from 0.001 to 0.0 over 15 epochs. (6) Early stopping (patience=3, min_delta=0.0) did not trigger because the model continued to achieve marginal improvements each epoch—consistent with the low-LR tail of the cosine schedule. (7) The best_configuration search-phase validation_accuracy (0.991004) differs from the final training run's best_val_accuracy (0.989804) by ~0.12%, which is within expected single-run variance (CUDA non-determinism, data-shuffle ordering) and does not indicate a defect. (8) The architecture_research stage carries action=revise with traceability gaps (tangential arxiv citation, null LLM digest, truncated text), but these are prior-stage administrative items that do not block the current training run; the configuration_replay stage independently confirmed the tiny_cnn config is sound. (9) official_test_separate_center=true is correctly flagged; downstream evaluation must report OOD/cross-center metrics separately from in-distribution results. (10) 28×28 RGB resolution class-ambiguity risks (background/debris/mucus, adipose vs. background, smooth muscle vs. stroma, lymphocytes vs. debris) should be surfaced via per-class metrics in the evaluation stage. No action-blocking issues identified; proceed to evaluation.
